(Per the Hon'ble the Chief Justice Alok Aradhe) Mr. K.Sai Sruthin Rao, learned counsel representing Mr. C. Hari Preeth, learned counsel for the petitioners.
Ms. L.Pranathi Reddy, learned counsel representing Mr. Gadi Praveen Kumar, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India, for respondents No.1 and 2.

Mr. D.Narendar Naik, learned counsel for respondent No.3.
2.

In this writ petition, the petitioners have prayed for the following relief:
For the reasons stated in the accompanying affidavit, it is prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to pass an order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the provisions of the Petroleum and Minerals (Pipelines, Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962, in so far as Sections 2, 3,
9(1) and 10(4) are illegal, arbitrary and unconstitutional under Article 14, 19, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India and consequently set aside the declaration issued u/s 6 of the Act published in Central Gazette in S.O.No.934 dt. 07-03-2005 and to restore back the possession taken in Sy.Nos.197 and 215 admeasuring Ac.1.11 gts and Ac.1.38 gts and from the 2nd petitioner in Sy. No.198 admeasuring Ac.1.05 gts situated at Shamirpet Village and Mandal, R.R.District and to pass such other order or orders as this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.
3.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Learned counsel for the parties jointly submit that the controversy involved in this writ petition is covered by an order dated 10.10.2023 passed by this Court in W.P.No.3414 of 2008.
4. In view of the aforesaid submission and for the reasons assigned by this Court in the aforesaid order dated 10.10.2023, the writ petition is disposed of with a direction to the Gas Transportation and Infrastructure Company Limited to make payment of compensation to the petitioners as determined by the competent authority under the provisions of the Petroleum and Minerals,
Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962, within a period one month from today.
Needless to state that in case the petitioners are aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, it will be open to them to take recourse to the remedy prescribed under Section 10(5) of the aforesaid Act.
It is also clarified that all contentions are kept open to be adjudicated in an appropriate proceeding.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
